q: Under hybrid icing, what decides whether icing is called?
a: Who reaches the faceoff dots first
o: Whether the goalie leaves his crease
sub: If the defender wins the race to the dots, icing is called. If the attacker wins, play goes on.

q: In which season did the NHL switch to hybrid icing?
sub: It came after Joni Pitkanen's career-ending crash into the boards while chasing an icing race.

q: When can a team ice the puck without icing being called?
o: When it leads by two goals
In the last minute of a period
sub: A team killing a penalty is allowed to fire the puck the length of the ice.

q: Since 2017-18, what is a team not allowed to do right after it ices the puck?
o: Take the faceoff with its centre
sub: That came on top of the ban on line changes after an icing, which started in 2005-06.

q: In which year did the NHL bring in the icing rule?
sub: A 1931 game in which the New York Americans iced the puck over 50 times helped push the change.

q: After an icing, where does the faceoff take place?
a: In the zone of the team that iced it
sub: Since 2019-20 the attacking team may also pick which of the two dots is used.

q: In the NHL, what happens to an icing if the goalie skates out of his crease towards the puck?
sub: Leaving the crease to play the puck means the goalie gave up the chance for a whistle.

q: Which body part decides whether an attacker is onside at the blue line?
sub: Both skates must be fully over the line before the puck for it to be offside. A stick cannot keep you on.

q: During a delayed offside, what must the attacking team do to avoid a whistle?
a: Tag up by leaving the zone
o: Touch the puck with a stick
sub: Once every attacker has touched back into the neutral zone, they can come back in.

q: If a linesman rules a team went offside on purpose, where is the faceoff?
sub: Intentional offside is punished by moving the faceoff all the way back.

q: Which is the one way a player can stay onside with both skates already over the blue line before the puck?
o: Holding his stick in the neutral zone
sub: A player carrying the puck backwards over the line is not ruled offside.

q: The centre red line was added in 1943-44. Whose idea was it, with Cecil Duncan?
sub: The red line let teams pass out of their own zone and sped up the game.

q: Which body scrapped the two-line pass rule in 1998, seven years before the NHL did?
sub: The NHL followed under its 2005 labour deal, after the lockout.

q: After which goalie, famous for playing the puck, is the NHL trapezoid rule nicknamed?
sub: Brought in for 2005-06, it limits where a goalie may handle the puck behind his net.

q: In which season did the trapezoid behind the goal first appear in the NHL?
sub: It was tested in the AHL in 2004-05 while the NHL was locked out.

q: What happens when an NHL goalie plays the puck behind the goal line outside the trapezoid?
sub: The trapezoid's goal-line side was widened by two feet on each side for 2014-15.

q: An NHL goalie gets a minor penalty if he plays the puck past which line?
sub: Patrick Roy was famously called for it in 1997 after a rush up the ice.

q: Who serves a penalty given to a goalie?
a: A teammate who was on the ice
sub: The penalty minutes still go on the goalie's own record.

q: In 2005-06 the NHL cut the maximum width of a goalie's leg pads to how much?
sub: Pads had been allowed to be 12 inches wide before the post-lockout crackdown.

q: In 2008 the NHL changed its rules after which player faced Martin Brodeur and waved his stick in his face?
sub: The Avery rule: such screening became an unsportsmanlike conduct minor the very next day.

q: Brett Hull's 1999 Cup winner was so disputed because of what?
a: His skate was in the crease
sub: After that season the automatic in-the-crease rule was dropped from the rulebook.

q: Can a goal count if the puck goes in off an attacker's skate?
a: Yes, unless he made a distinct kicking motion
sub: Video review checks for a deliberate kick. A puck that just bounces in off a skate is a goal.

q: A goal tipped in with a stick is disallowed when the stick touched the puck above what?
sub: For tips straight into the net, the crossbar, 4 feet up, is the limit.

q: In which zone is a hand pass to a teammate allowed in the NHL?
sub: Anywhere else, a hand pass to a teammate stops play for a faceoff.

q: How high is the crossbar of an NHL goal above the ice?
sub: The goal mouth is 6 feet wide and 4 feet high.

q: If a defender fouls a skater on a breakaway after his team pulled its goalie, what is given?
sub: With nobody in net, there's no point taking the shot, so the goal simply counts.

q: What happens to the minor penalty when a penalty shot is given instead?
sub: Whether the shot goes in or not, the minor is not served.

q: What does a player usually get for a high stick that draws blood?
sub: It's custom more than a written rule, and referees can use their judgement.

q: A power-play goal ends a minor penalty. Which penalty does a goal not end early?
sub: On a major the team can score again and again for the full five minutes.

q: A team scores 15 seconds into an opponent's double minor. How much is left on the penalty?
sub: A goal only ends the current two-minute block of a double minor.

q: Montreal's power play was so deadly that a goal ending a minor penalty began after which season?
sub: Jean Beliveau scored three power-play goals in 44 seconds on 5 November 1955.

q: When two players get minor penalties at the same time in the NHL, how do teams play?
sub: Matching minors leave both teams a skater short until the penalties end.

q: How many skaters must a team always keep on the ice, however many penalties it takes?
sub: Extra penalties are stacked and start only when an earlier one runs out.

q: How many penalty minutes go on a player's record in the NHL for a game misconduct?
sub: He is thrown out of the game, but his team does not play shorthanded for it.

q: What happens to a delayed minor penalty if the fouled team scores before play stops?
o: It goes to the next period
sub: That's why teams pull the goalie on a delayed call: a goal costs them nothing.

q: Since 1992, what extra penalty does the NHL give the player who starts a fight?
sub: He gets the extra 2 minutes on top of his 5-minute fighting major.

q: What happens to a player who instigates a fight in the last five minutes of an NHL game?
sub: His coach is fined $10,000 too, and both double for each repeat.

q: Since 1971, what happens to the first player who joins a fight already going on?
a: He is thrown out of the game
sub: This is the third man in rule.

q: Who breaks up fights on the ice in the NHL?
sub: The referees keep other players away and write down the penalties.

q: How is fighting treated in Olympic hockey?
a: It is banned and leads to ejection
sub: The IIHF rulebook says fighting is not a part of international hockey.

q: Since 2019-20, what must an NHL skater do if his helmet comes off during play?
a: Put it back on or go to the bench
o: Stop and wait for a whistle
sub: Stay in the play bareheaded and he gets a 2-minute minor.

q: What does an NHL team get for two faceoff violations on the same faceoff?
a: A bench minor for delay of game
o: The faceoff moved to its zone
sub: The first violation just gets the centre thrown out of the circle.

q: In which season did the NHL bring in the coach's challenge?
sub: It was for goals that might have come after an offside or goalie interference.

q: What does the Trushinski bylaw keep out of the NHL?
sub: Frank Trushinski lost sight in one eye in 1921 and later most of the other.

q: How many timeouts does each NHL team get in a game?
sub: It can only be called at a normal stoppage of play.

q: Which team gets the last line change before a faceoff?
o: The team on the power play
sub: The visitors must put their players out first, so the home coach can match lines.

q: At a centre-ice faceoff in the NHL, which centre must put his stick down first?
o: The one who lost the last draw
The one on the power play
sub: In the end zones, the defending centre goes first.

q: In which season did NHL regular-season overtime return, after being dropped in 1942?
sub: The Islanders won the first one, 8-7 over Washington on 8 October 1983.

q: In which season did the NHL start giving a point for an overtime loss, with 4-on-4 overtime?
sub: The AHL had tried 4-on-4 overtime a season earlier.

q: If a team pulls its goalie in regular-season overtime and gives up an empty-net goal, what does it lose?
sub: So coaches rarely pull the goalie in overtime, except for a delayed penalty.

q: How many shooters does each team get in an NHL shootout before sudden death?
sub: After that, it goes round by round until one team scores and the other misses.

q: In an NHL shootout, when can a player shoot a second time?
a: Once every skater on the roster has shot
sub: Goalies don't count, so in a long shootout every skater gets a turn.

q: Who decides whether a team shoots first in an NHL shootout?
sub: Most home coaches choose to shoot first.

q: Which Florida player ended the NHL's 20-round shootout against Washington in December 2014?
sub: The old record had been 15 rounds.

q: Which move was banned from NHL shootouts and penalty shots in 2014-15?
sub: The league said a full spin made it hard to tell if the shooter kept moving forward.

q: Which Detroit player ended the 1936 sextuple-overtime game, the longest NHL game ever played?
sub: He scored at 116:30 of overtime to beat the Montreal Maroons 1-0.

q: How is the Olympic and World Championship gold-medal game decided if tied?
sub: The IIHF uses 3-on-3 for all its overtimes, and the final has no shootout.

q: In which season did the NHL make two referees per game compulsory?
sub: The four-official system was trialled in some games from 1998-99.

q: How far is the goal line from the end boards on an NHL rink?
sub: IIHF rinks put it 4 metres from the boards.

q: How wide is the neutral zone between the blue lines on an NHL rink?
sub: Each blue line sits 75 feet from its end boards.

q: How long is an international IIHF rink?
sub: It can be 26 to 30 metres wide, wider than the NHL's 85 feet.

q: Which colour is the centre faceoff circle, unlike the other eight spots?
sub: All the other faceoff circles and spots are red.

q: How much does a regulation NHL puck weigh?
sub: 5.5 to 6 ounces, made of black vulcanised rubber, 3 inches across.

q: What colour is the light 4-ounce puck made for young children?
sub: Heavier pink or orange pucks of 10 ounces are used to train shot strength.

q: In Kingston in 1886, what was the hockey puck made from?
sub: Being soft rubber, it bounced far more than modern pucks.

q: What did the FoxTrax puck, first used at the 1996 All-Star Game, do on TV?
a: Showed a glowing streak behind it
sub: The blue streak turned red on very hard shots. Fans of the game mostly hated it.

q: What is a Texas hat trick?
sub: Everything's bigger in Texas. The term was in print by 1969.

q: Which player is credited with the most Gordie Howe hat tricks in NHL history?
sub: He is credited with 18.

q: In 1952, Bill Mosienko scored the fastest hat trick in NHL history. How long did it take?
sub: He did it for the Chicago Black Hawks against the New York Rangers.

q: In which sport was the term hat-trick first used, in 1858?
sub: H. H. Stephenson took three wickets with three balls, and fans bought him a hat.

q: Which Florida player killed a rat in the locker room in 1995, then scored twice that night?
sub: Goalie John Vanbiesbrouck called it a rat trick, and fans began throwing rats.

q: In January 2026, NHL players set a record for hat tricks in one month. How many?
sub: The old record was 29, from December 1985.

q: Where on the net is 'where mama hides the cookies'?
sub: High in the net, just under the crossbar, like a top kitchen shelf.

q: In hockey, what is Gretzky's office?
a: The area behind the opponent's net
sub: Gretzky loved to set up plays from behind the net.

q: In hockey slang, what are chiclets?
sub: Spitting chiclets means losing teeth after a hit.

q: In hockey slang, what is a bucket?
sub: A helmet is also called a lid.

q: What is a bender in hockey slang?
a: A weak skater whose ankles bend inward
o: A long night out after a win
sub: It's one of the oldest insults in the dressing room.

q: What is a plumber in hockey slang?
a: A gritty player who does the dirty work
o: A goalie who plays deep in his net
sub: Also called a mucker or a pipe-fitter.

q: What is a goon in hockey?
a: A player whose main job is fighting
sub: Goons were most common in the 1970s and 1980s.

q: In hockey slang, what is a gino?
sub: Also spelt geno.

q: What is a muffin in hockey slang?
sub: An easy one for the goalie to swallow.

q: What is a yard sale in hockey?
a: A player losing his gear after a big hit
sub: Stick, gloves and helmet lie scattered on the ice.

q: Why are referees called zebras?
sub: Officials wear black-and-white striped shirts.

q: In hockey slang, what are mitts?
sub: A player with great mitts has very good hands.

q: In hockey slang, what are the pipes?
sub: A goalie is said to play between the pipes.

q: In hockey slang, what is the paint?
sub: It's the blue-painted area in front of the goal.

q: In hockey slang, what is a tilly?
sub: Other words for a fight include a dance and a donnybrook.

q: What is a gong show in hockey?
a: A wild game full of goals, fights and penalties
sub: It can also describe a player who is out of control.

q: In hockey slang, what is lettuce or salad?
sub: Also called flow.

q: What is a snow shower in hockey?
a: Spraying ice shavings on a goalie with a hard stop
sub: Do it after the whistle and expect a crowd around you.

q: What is a bottle rocket in hockey?
a: A shot that knocks the goalie's water bottle off the net
sub: Some call it a bottle knocker.

q: What does it mean to get Kronwalled?
a: To be flattened by a big open-ice hit
o: To be scored on through the legs
To be traded at the deadline
sub: Named after Detroit's Swedish defenceman Niklas Kronwall.

q: How is a Michigan, or lacrosse goal, scored?
a: Scooping up the puck and tucking it in from behind the net
sub: Named after Michigan's Mike Legg, who did it in an NCAA tournament game in 1996.

q: Who scored the first lacrosse-style Michigan goal in the NHL, in October 2019?
sub: He did it against Calgary on 29 October 2019, and again that December.

q: Which Canadiens defenceman is the spin-o-rama said to be named after?
sub: Commentator Danny Gallivan coined it. Denis Savard made it famous later.

q: What is a coast-to-coast goal?
a: A player carries the puck the length of the rink and scores
o: A goal on a road trip
A goal from the opponent's mistake
sub: One player beats the whole team on his own.

q: What is tic-tac-toe in hockey?
a: Three quick passes leading to a goal
sub: Done right, the goalie has no chance.

q: What is a tape-to-tape pass?
a: A pass right onto a teammate's stick blade
sub: Players wrap tape around the blade of their stick.

q: What is a flamingo in hockey?
a: Lifting a leg to dodge a shot
sub: Usually a skater who doesn't fancy blocking the shot.

q: When a defenceman pinches, what is he doing?
a: Moving up to keep the puck in the attacking zone
sub: Pinch at the wrong time and you leave your team open to an odd-man rush.

q: What is a hoser, in Canadian slang?
sub: Made famous by Bob and Doug McKenzie of SCTV.

q: What is a howitzer in hockey?
sub: Named after a big artillery gun.

q: What is the slot?
a: The area in front of the goalie between the faceoff circles
o: The gap between the bench and the boards
sub: It is the best place on the ice to score from.

q: What is a dump and chase?
a: Shooting the puck deep and racing to win it back
sub: Teams use it to get past a strong blue-line defence.

q: What is a pest in hockey?
a: A player who annoys opponents to throw them off
o: A rookie who talks too much
sub: Pests try to draw the other team into penalties.

q: How long do other NHL teams get to claim a player put on waivers?
sub: Claims open at noon Mountain Time and close a day later.

q: If several NHL teams claim the same player on waivers in mid-season, who gets him?
a: The team lowest in the standings
o: The team with most cap space
sub: Before 1 November, last season's standings decide.

q: What kind of salary cap does the NHL use, with no luxury tax option?
sub: No team may go over it at all, unlike baseball or the NBA.

q: At what level did the NHL salary cap stay flat through the COVID-hit seasons?
sub: It finally rose again for 2022-23.

q: What does a team get if it does not match another team's offer sheet for its player?
sub: The value of the picks depends on the size of the offer.

q: In which year did the NHL bring in the draft lottery?
sub: At first only teams that missed the playoffs could take part.

q: Under the NHL lottery rules from 2022, how many places can a lottery winner move up at most?
sub: So only the bottom 11 teams can win the first pick.

q: How many regular-season games did each team play in the lockout-shortened 1994-95 and 2012-13 seasons?
sub: Both seasons had no games between the two conferences.
